why-charholi-pcmc.title: Why Buy a Home in Charholi, PCMC Pune | Tanish Urbania
why-charholi-pcmc.desc: What makes Charholi near Ajinkya D.Y. Patil University a practical address in PCMC, Pune, and what to check before you decide on a home.
why-charholi-pcmc.body:
Charholi sits in the Pimpri-Chinchwad Municipal Corporation (PCMC) belt of Pune, close to Ajinkya D.Y. Patil University. It is one of the parts of the city that is developing fastest, with new infrastructure and landmark projects coming up in the surrounding area.

What buyers look for in a growing corridor

A growing corridor tends to bring three things together: better road and public connectivity, more day-to-day services, and a steady stream of new residential communities. Together they usually make a neighbourhood easier to live in as time passes.

Where Tanish Urbania fits

Tanish Urbania is planned as a contemporary residential community in this corridor, with 12 residential wings, landscaped open areas and lifestyle amenities. The aim is a home that offers comfort and connectivity today and long-term value later.

Before you decide

Visit the area at different times of the day, check the routes you would take to work or school, and ask the sales team for the current list of nearby facilities. Seeing the neighbourhood yourself tells you more than any brochure.

2-bhk-vs-3-bhk.title: 2 BHK vs 3 BHK: How to Choose | Tanish Urbania
2-bhk-vs-3-bhk.desc: Comparing 2 BHK and 3 BHK homes in Charholi, Pune: sizes, who each suits, and questions to ask before you choose. Tanish Urbania buying guide.
2-bhk-vs-3-bhk.body:
Choosing between a 2 BHK and a 3 BHK is mostly a question of how you live today and how you expect to live in five to ten years.

The 2 BHK case

At Tanish Urbania, 2 BHK homes are approximately 720 to 770 sq ft. This size suits couples, small families and first-time buyers who want an efficient layout, a lower purchase price and lower running costs.

The 3 BHK case

3 BHK homes are approximately 920 to 980 sq ft. The extra bedroom works as a children’s room, a guest room or a home office, which is why many families prefer it if they plan to work from home or expect the household to grow.

Questions to ask yourself

  • Will someone work from home most days?
  • Do parents or guests stay with you often?
  • How long do you plan to live here?
  • What monthly EMI is comfortable for you?

If you are unsure, register your interest and our team will share floor plans so you can compare the two layouts side by side.

buying-a-pre-launch-home-checklist.title: Pre-Launch Home Buying Checklist, Pune | Tanish Urbania
buying-a-pre-launch-home-checklist.desc: A six-point checklist for buying a flat before launch in Pune: RERA registration, approved plans, payment schedule, possession date and total cost.
buying-a-pre-launch-home-checklist.body:
Buying early can give you access to good options, but it also asks you to check a few things carefully. Use this list for any upcoming project, including ours.

Six checks

  • RERA registration. Confirm the project’s registration number and details on the MahaRERA website.
  • Developer track record. Look at earlier projects and how they were delivered.
  • Approved plans. Ask to see the sanctioned plans and the carpet area of your unit.
  • Payment schedule. Get the full schedule in writing, with all charges listed.
  • Possession timeline. Note the committed date in the agreement.
  • Total cost. Ask for the all-inclusive price, including taxes, registration and maintenance deposits.

Take your time

A good developer will answer these questions openly. Tanish Urbania is launching soon; register your interest and our team will share the details as they are confirmed.

light-and-ventilation-in-apartment-desig.title: Light and Ventilation in Apartment Design | Tanish Urbania
light-and-ventilation-in-apartment-desig.desc: How wing placement, balconies and open areas improve daylight and cross ventilation in a modern residential community in Charholi, Pune.
light-and-ventilation-in-apartment-desig.body:
A home can look good on a plan and still feel closed in. Light, air and open space depend on how the buildings are placed as much as on how each flat is laid out.

Wing placement

Tanish Urbania has 12 residential wings positioned to leave ample open space between them. That spacing helps daylight reach the homes and lets air move through the site.

Balconies and cross ventilation

Generous balconies extend the living space outdoors, and layouts planned for cross ventilation keep rooms fresher with less reliance on fans and air conditioning.

Open and landscaped areas

Well-distributed landscaped zones give residents somewhere to walk, sit and meet neighbours, while the master plan keeps a level of privacy for each home.

The design comes from YW Architects, with a modern language of clean geometry, vertical accents and balanced proportions.
